title: Paired-traffic throttle experiment engine and adaptive rollback policy
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Deliver a product-quality A/B experimentation engine that uses paired (mirrored) requests with configurable throttling to control exposure, adaptive sequential statistical checks to stop early, and automated rollback hooks tied to operational and quality gates. This ticket covers the product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout UX, and coordination points with engineering for implementation and telemetry.

Scope:
- Paired traffic mode: mirror a sampled subset of live requests to a candidate model while returning baseline responses to users. Candidate outputs are recorded for metric computation and side-by-side comparison.
- Throttle/knob model: exposure expressed as a paired-mirror ratio (e.g., 1%, 5%, 20%) with a traffic-throttle token bucket to prevent bursty jumps.
- Adaptive stopping: sequential hypothesis testing (alpha-spend scheduler) with per-cohort stratified checks and multi-metric composite scoring.
- Auto-rollback: automatic rollback and incident trigger when pre-defined safety gates breach (statistical degradation, error spikes, latency regressions).
- Console UX: guided experiment creation, cohort selection, and live health dashboard with rollback controls and rationale logs.
acceptance_criteria: Product UI to create paired-mirror experiments with exposure knobs (mirror ratio, duration, cohorts)
Experiment controller supports adaptive alpha-spend sequential checks and emits stop/continue decisions to infra
Telemetry schema captures paired request id, baseline candidate pair outcome, error codes, latency ms, tokens used
Auto-rollback action defined and exercised in a staging run: rollback triggers when posterior prob(candidate worse) > 0.95 for primary metric
Docs + runbook for SRE/operators describing rollback signals and manual override steps
tasks: Finalize product spec and UX flows (this ticket)
Design telemetry events and storage schema (ENG-21455)
Implement traffic-throttle token bucket in routing layer (ENG-22001)
Build sequential statistic engine (ENG-22102) and integrate with rollout controller
Console: experiment form, visualization, and rollback button
E2E test using canary cluster with synthetic traffic and shadow mirror
Write runbook and postmortem template for automated rollbacks
updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting — product, eng, and design aligned on paired-mirror as default safe test mode. Decided to treat paired experiments as non-user-facing by default (baseline responses served).

2026-02-25: Design proposal uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/MODEL/Paired+Traffic+Throttle+Spec (link preview). Key change: add per-cohort throttle so we can ramp on low-risk cohorts first.
2026-03-02: Eng spike complete — prototype token-bucket throttle implemented in the routing shim. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/642 (prototype).

2026-03-06: Statistical approach approved — sequential Bayes with alpha-spend schedule and Holm correction for multiple metrics. Agreed primary metric = user-perceived quality score and safety metric = per-request error delta.
2026-03-10: Wireframes for console flows ready. UX note: require a short rationale + rollback policy when creating an experiment to ensure operational clarity.
decision_log: Paired vs shadow: choose paired mirror (candidate evaluated but baseline responses returned) to minimize user risk while capturing full fidelity comparison.
Stat testing: adopt Bayesian sequential testing with an alpha-spend schedule instead of fixed-sample frequentist t-tests to allow early stopping and continuous monitoring.

Auto-rollback thresholds: use probability-based trigger (posterior P(candidate < baseline) > 0.95) OR operational trigger (absolute error-rate increase > 1% AND p95 latency reg > 50ms) to avoid noisy rollbacks.
Cohorts: stratify by locale and latency bucket to catch regressions that only appear in specific slices.
risk_and_mitigation: Key risks: 1) False positives due to multiple metrics and correlated signals — mitigation: conservative alpha-spend and composite metric weighting, plus manual review gate for major rollbacks. 2) Storage and cost for mirrored payloads — mitigation: sample payloads, redact PII, and enforce TTL. 3) Burst exposure spikes — mitigation: token-bucket throttle and circuit-breaker that resets mirror flow on sudden error-rate uptick.
notes: Implementation notes for ENG: emit a paired_request_id for every mirrored request, index numeric metrics in time-series DB with cohort tags, implement offline comparator job for heavy metrics. Consider using off-policy evaluation for quality signals where ground truth is available. Ensure KMS/Audit logging for candidate artifacts in Private deployments.
